players.product: High-density AI data-center colocation / powered infrastructure (ex-Bitcoin-mining conversion)

quarterly_data.signal: No new colocation customer was signed by the Q4 call (CEO: 'we are not satisfied with that'), which management called a timing issue, not a demand issue: hyperscalers would not engage while the merger agreement was in place and talks restarted after its termination. Two sites are under short exclusivity arrangements - 500 MW under exclusivity with a large investment-grade counterparty - and active discussions span hyperscalers, neoclouds and large enterprises. Neocloud deals need a strong balance sheet behind the contract - in most cases a hyperscaler, chip manufacturer or other investment-grade guarantee.
quarterly_data.figure: 500 megawatts under exclusivity arrangements with a large investment-grade counterparty; 2 sites under short exclusivity

quarterly_data.signal: Power/site expansion: Dalton, Georgia will expand to 450 MW of total gross power capacity including 120 MW of uncommitted leasable customer capacity (additional 175 acres secured). Pecos, Texas leasable capacity was raised to 200 MW and Pecos is being converted from Bitcoin mining to colocation (general contractor secured, long-lead equipment locked in, RFS within 12 months). Contract signed to acquire a new Hunt County, Texas site (approximately 265 acres, roughly 430 MW gross / 285 MW customer-leasable, about 45 miles outside Dallas), expected to close by end of Q1; its ERCOT energization schedule was approved in 2024 with power coming online in 2027 and ramping through 2029, and management said it is not impacted by Senate Bill 6 and will not be restudied by ERCOT.
quarterly_data.figure: Dalton 450 megawatts gross incl. 120 megawatts uncommitted leasable; Pecos 200 megawatts leasable; Hunt roughly 430 megawatts gross / 285 megawatts leasable (approximately 265 acres)

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline of approximately 1.5 gigawatts of customer leasable capacity (management: not speculative, not inflated with load studies). Management said power is often overstated as the bottleneck - the bigger constraints are securing long-lead equipment and lining up experienced general contractors and subcontractors; 'We already have more power in our pipeline than we can build over the next several years.' Internal capacity to build as much as 500 megawatts in a single calendar year, dependent on customers stepping in early to line up financing and supply chain. Expects every megawatt in the portfolio to be dedicated to colocation within the next 3 years.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 1.5 gigawatts pipeline; as much as 500 megawatts buildable in a single calendar year

quarterly_data.signal: 'Operation Forward Observer' go-to-market: advance sites through the first commissioned data hall and secure long-lead equipment before contract signing. Sites: Hunt campus (285 leasable MW near Dallas-Fort Worth, initial delivery 2H 2027); Pecos Phase 1 (185 MW leasable, initial delivery early 2027); Dalton Phase 3 (approximately 250,000 sq ft, 120 MW leasable, initial delivery 2H 2027); Auburn, Alabama (30 MW leasable Tier 3 multi-tenant site, first 10 MW in 2H 2026, aimed at inference and enterprise customers). Development pipeline expanded by 600 leasable megawatts.
quarterly_data.figure: Pecos Phase 1 185 megawatts (early 2027); Dalton Phase 3 120 megawatts (2H 2027); Auburn first 10 megawatts (2H 2026); pipeline expanded by 600 leasable megawatts

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing: lease rates have continued to move higher, driven by rising equipment and labor prices; management expects 'a touch movement higher' in 2026 but not a material move, since hyperscalers price on a yield against their basis-of-design cost. Hyperscalers expect capacity delivered sub-18 months and in some cases sub-12 months; time to RFS is 'the trump card' for pricing, and sites near major metros (e.g. Hunt) command stronger pricing.

Design is adapting to each GPU generation: the first CoreWeave data center started with H100, then NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVL36s and NVL72s, then GB200 to GB300 platforms, with data halls adapted in flight; NVIDIA's Vera Rubin reference architecture is now being factored into new projects for cooling and power distribution. Management is also evaluating standardized designs adaptable to Google TPUs as they become more prevalent outside the Google ecosystem. Dalton Phase 1 is being prepared for high-density liquid-cooled AI systems.

2025 was a transitional year: the vast majority of revenue still came from Bitcoin mining (now 'essentially in runoff', run to meet minimum power draw requirements; hash price dipped below $0.03), and colocation revenue is expected to reach an inflection in the coming months. Year-end total liquidity of approximately $530 million; sold just over 1,900 Bitcoin for approximately $175 million in January and holds under 1,000 Bitcoin. Pipeline sites to use project financing with a 60% to 85% advance rate on build costs. A historical restatement (2024 onward) wrote off demolished PP&E from mining-site conversions, with no impact to revenue, adjusted EBITDA or net cash flow; a material weakness will be noted for the next 4 quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: total liquidity of approximately $530 million; just over 1,900 Bitcoin sold for approximately $175 million; 60% to 85% advance rate

quarterly_data.signal: Management on guarantees: neocloud and AI-lab deal signing changed dramatically in Q3 2025 as guarantees were introduced (some deals backed by Google); guarantees range from debt guarantees to full lease guarantees, and management expects hyperscalers and all chip manufacturers to provide guarantees for neoclouds and labs to lock in their architecture, with terms centralizing over 2026. Core Scientific is negotiating with certain guarantee counterparties (not named).

connects_to.relationship: Dedicated AI data-center capacity leased to CoreWeave (12-year leases across 5+ sites)

contracts.signal: CoreWeave build-out progress: 5 AI factories broken ground for the 590-megawatt CoreWeave commitment (Denton TX, Marble NC, Muskogee OK, Dalton Phase 1 and Phase 2 GA). 213 MW energized by end of calendar 2025 (one data hall short of goal); as of the call approximately 350 MW energized with close to 200 MW billing (billing generally within 90 days of energization). Denton (262 MW campus) delivered 67 billable MW by end of Q4 and now represents approximately 130 billable MW supporting more than 50,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs, full campus by midyear; Marble (65 MW) has 36 billable MW supporting approximately 15,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs, final hall in Q2; Muskogee Phase 1 (70 MW) and Dalton Phase 1 (30 MW) energized, full delivery in Q2; Dalton Phase 2 (145 MW) targeted early 2027 as the final CoreWeave site. Full contract expected delivered going into early 2027.
contracts.units: 590-megawatt commitment; approximately 350 megawatts energized, close to 200 megawatts billing; 213 megawatts energized at end of 2025; more than 50,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs at Denton; approximately 15,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs at Marble

contracts.signal: CFO: the 590 MW CoreWeave contract represents between $5 billion and $5.5 billion of total infrastructure; Core Scientific can raise up to $4 billion against its contracted CoreWeave capacity at full stabilization, a good portion of which is borrowable today, with the vast majority expected before the end of this year. COO: in 2025 the 5 CoreWeave sites represented nearly $2 billion of installed infrastructure assets and over $5 billion in total project investment.
contracts.value: $5 billion and $5.5 billion of total infrastructure; up to $4 billion financing capacity
